absent: Full field layouts of open file, open node, node, operations and sequential file structures beyond fields referenced in these fragments.
Acquisition, release and lifetime rules for active references and node references.
Backend callback contracts for read, write, map, poll, seek, open, release and sequential display.
Complete lock ordering and interrupt context rules beyond the nesting and protection notes shown.
Numeric values of error codes, poll masks, fault codes and whence constants.
Mount, superblock, inode and dentry management for kernfs instances.
Behavior of stubbed allocation, iterator, list, atomic, RCU and diagnostic helpers.

findings.text: Sequential file service exposes a read iterator and a release operation usable by filesystem file operations for generated content.
Generic seek service exposes position query and update helpers that resolve whence against end of file and enforce upper and lower bounds.
Kernfs core exposes a notification trigger, a generic poll helper, and a file operations table wiring standard file methods to kernfs handlers.

Kernfs file objects are entered through a single operations table that routes read, write, seek, memory map, open, release and poll requests to dedicated handlers, with read further routed to sequential or direct handling based on a node capability flag.

Direct kernfs read service guarantees at most one page of backend data per call, serialized per open file, valid only while the node stays active, with the caller event snapshot refreshed from shared open state and file position advanced only after successful delivery to the caller iterator. Deactivation, missing backend, allocation failure and transfer fault are reported distinctly.

Kernfs write service enforces a per file atomic limit when configured and otherwise a single page limit, requires successful capture from the caller iterator with string termination assurance, serializes backend invocation per open file while active, and advances position only on positive backend result.

Kernfs memory mapping wrappers require configured backend mapping operations and an active open file, otherwise signaling bus or invalid argument failure. Fault handling defaults to bus failure when the backend lacks a fault callback, while write fault handling updates file times when no backend callback exists.

Mapping establishment checks a node mapping capability without locking, then under the per open mutex and active guard delegates to the backend mapper, rejects file substitution, mixed backend operations across mappings of the same open file, and backends requesting close interception, and on first success records mapping state and installs wrapper operations.

Open handling requires an active node, derives readable writable and mappable capabilities from backend callbacks, optionally enforces extra permission checks against mode bits, caches the atomic write limit outside the active guard, forbids combining preallocation with sequential display, always instantiates sequential file state, restores write position capability when appropriate, and unwinds node linkage and allocations on failure.

Shared open state per node is created lazily with an initial event generation, a poll queue and an empty file list, published for concurrent readers, extended with each opener and release accounting when the node needs release handling, and reclaimed only after the last opener detaches, with mapped and release counters adjusted symmetrically.
Sequential file buffer allocation refuses sizes beyond the global read write maximum and otherwise obtains kernel accounted memory that can grow by doubling on overflow.

Sequential file positioning treats zero as a reset to the first record, detects divergence between requested position and last read position and rewalks records from the start to resynchronize, discarding accumulated state with prejudice on walk failure.
Kernfs seek handling serializes per open file under active guard and prefers a backend seek callback when present, falling back to the generic seek implementation.

Generic whence resolution maps end relative requests by adding end of file, treats zero displacement current position queries as pure reads without rewriting position, validates data and hole requests against end of file, and maps valid hole requests to end of file.

Position installation rejects negative values unless unsigned offsets are allowed and rejects values beyond the filesystem maximum, updates stored position only on change, and optionally clears an associated cookie.

Poll handling registers the caller on the shared open poll queue and reports a changed event generation as error and priority alongside the default mask, with backend specific poll preferred when implemented and deactivation reported as error and priority.

Notification immediately bumps the shared event generation and wakes poll waiters under read side protection when open state exists, and enqueues the node at most once on a global list with a reference held before scheduling deferred filesystem notification work that emits modify events per mounted superblock.

Per open file mutex nests outside the active reference and serializes backend read, write, seek and map calls for the same open file, with mapping capability prechecked without the mutex to avoid false lock ordering warnings.

A dedicated preallocation mutex protects the reusable per open buffer across concurrent read and write operations, held only while the shared buffer is in use and released before return, with private allocations using no such protection.
Sequential file lock serializes all iterator, buffer, index and position state for a read, held across buffer draining, record production and copying to the caller.

Global notification list is protected by an interrupt safe spinlock with enqueue guarded against duplicates, while deferred work iterates superblocks under nested read locks for supers and filesystem state.
Per node open file mutex serializes creation, linkage, counter updates and reclamation of shared open state, with publication and lookup using read copy update primitives.

Sequential read progresses through position validation, buffer reuse, record acquisition with skip and overflow handling including buffer doubling and restart, optional multi record packing bounded by caller demand, and final position advancement, with empty output mapped to either transfer fault or the last hard error.

Open file lifecycle moves from active acquisition through capability derivation, allocation, sequential state setup, shared node linkage and backend open, to steady use, then to release handling with counter adjustment, node unlinking and staged freeing of sequential state and buffers.

Notification queueing moves a node from idle to queued with a held reference, to deferred processing that fans out to superblocks and releases the reference, repeating until a sentinel indicates emptiness.

Sequential iteration assumes backend start, show, next and stop callbacks cooperate. A next callback that leaves the position index unchanged is detected and corrected with a rate limited diagnostic, while overflow triggers buffer doubling that can fail with out of memory.

Mapping rejects backends that substitute the mapped file, mix operations across mappings, or request close wrapping, since close wrapping cannot be implemented safely. Open rejects simultaneous preallocation and sequential display because sequential reads manage their own allocation.
Backend invocation after deactivation is unsafe. All paths revalidate activity under the per open mutex or equivalent guard and report device absence or bus fault without calling the backend.
Kernfs persistent file operations layout provides slots for read iterator, write iterator, seek, map, open, release, poll, sync and splice read and write.
Kernfs mapping operations layout provides slots for open, fault, write fault and access wrappers.
Direct kernfs read and default write and preallocation bound is a single PAGE_SIZE unit, with a configured atomic write length overriding that bound and oversize atomic writes rejected with E2BIG.
Generic seek understands SEEK_END and SEEK_CUR and SEEK_DATA and SEEK_HOLE with whole file data semantics and hole at end of file.
Poll change signaling combines DEFAULT_POLLMASK with EPOLLERR and EPOLLPRI.
Absent mapping backend or inactive mapping use during fault handling is reported as VM_FAULT_SIGBUS, while equivalent failure during synchronous access is reported as EINVAL.
Sequential buffer allocation fails when the requested size exceeds MAX_RW_COUNT.
